definition: Parallel scan, also known as parallel prefix sum, is an algorithm used to compute prefix sums efficiently in parallel.
details: Parallel scan, also known as parallel prefix sum, is an algorithm used to compute prefix sums efficiently in parallel. It's useful in applications where you need to perform computations on large data arrays in a parallel computing environment.

explainer.lead: Parallel scan, also called parallel prefix sum, computes all prefix sums of an array efficiently in parallel. It matters because it turns an apparently sequential accumulation into a parallel primitive used on large data arrays.

tiers.eli5: Each person in a line adds up everyone in front of them at once, instead of passing a running total down the line one by one.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use parallel scan as a building block in parallel computing environments where prefix computations over large arrays are needed. A pitfall is that the extra work stages of a parallel scan can cost more than a simple serial loop on small or poorly balanced inputs.
tiers.paperLevel: Parallel scan, also known as parallel prefix sum, is an algorithm used to compute prefix sums efficiently in parallel; it is useful in applications needing computations on large data arrays in a parallel computing environment.

explainer.example: Given the array [3, 1, 4, 2], the parallel prefix sum produces [3, 4, 8, 10] using staged pairwise combinations rather than four sequential steps.
